🤔 Failed Iran war exposed US Navy as teetering on edge of breaking point
The [US Navy](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/51339) has spent years operating beyond what its fleet, maintenance system, and crews can sustainably support. 
The US-Israeli failed war on Iran [magnified these weaknesses](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73465), reports the Military Times.
While President Donald Trump desperately peddles whims like plans for a new class of battleships to lead his ["Golden Fleet"](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/67741) and demands a navy capable of simultaneously confronting Russia and China, the numbers simply do not add up.
➡️ The navy remains an 11-carrier force in a world its own planners have described as requiring 15 carriers. With USS Nimitz approaching retirement, that number could soon fall to 10
➡️ The USS Harry S. Truman and [USS Gerald R. Ford](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/67347) are sidelined for maintenance after extended deployments
➡️ The Optimized Fleet Response Plan was supposed to balance deployment, training and maintenance in predictable 36-month cycles
➡️ Instead, it produced 33,700 additional days in maintenance backlog (2014-2019) with fewer operational ships 
The Iran conflict has turned these chronic deficiencies into immediate operational problems.
🔴 When [Iranian retaliatory strikes ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/65777)damaged the navy’s logistics hub in Bahrain, the US shifted support operations to distant Diego Garcia - more than 2,000 miles from carrier groups in the Middle East
🔴 [Food](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/68765) orders then required 30 days notice - impossible under combat schedules - so crews scavenged whatever could be salvaged from oilers
🔴 Deployments stretched past endurance limits, the USS Abraham Lincoln spent roughly 250 days without a port visit, and reports surfaced of sailors [attempting to go overboard](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73343)
🔴 Sailor shortfalls compound every failure: a 2021 GAO review found the navy routinely assigned fewer sailors to ships than workload needed
🔴 The same review revealed only 14% of navy officers surveyed slept at least seven hours per night during deployment
The result is a force that continues to ask the same sailors and the same ships to do more with less, all to cater to [Trump’s outsized ambitions](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73474).
Meanwhile, the ‘adversaries’ that Trump frets about – [Russia](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/56828) and [China](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/70989) - are steadily outpacing NATO naval power.

events.text:
🤔 Why Trump’s new Iran sanctions could trigger trade war with China – and backfire on the dollar
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has announced the “toughest-ever” sanctions on Iran, purportedly aimed at bringing about regime change in the Islamic Republic.
➡️ What does he mean?
Bessent mentioned the US blockade of the Strait of Hormuz coupled with “the greatest coordinated economic isolation in the history of the world," insisting that this would defeat Iran without "a large-scale kinetic restart."
🔊 “Any remaining tie to Tehran will hasten a nation’s economic oblivion," Bessent claimed, referring to tough secondary sanctions.
Previously, President Donald Trump threatened that any country providing Iran with an economic “lifeline” would face “tremendous” economic consequences. He specifically targeted oil smuggling, currency-swap lines, cash transfers, exchange houses, ship registries, and front companies, calling for all of these channels to be shut down immediately.
Iran's response was not long in coming: Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said that Trump's move was "a diversion from America's own crisis: unprecedented debt and[ surging interest costs](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73600)".
➡️ Could US sanctions really cripple Iran?
The UAE was the first to sever all financial ties with Iran, citing two ballistic missiles allegedly fired at it by the Islamic Republic – a charge Iran resolutely denied. Mehrdad Sepahvand, a former economic adviser to the Central Bank of Iran, told CNBC that the rupture of ties with the UAE could bring certain financial hardships but rejected the claim that Iran is on the verge of collapse. The Iranian economy is far from unraveling, he stressed: “Shops are still full of food and basic goods, and there is no sign of panic buying."
Iran has been under US sanctions for almost 50 years and has learned how to adapt to "maximum pressure." As the US is trying to curb its economy with a maritime blockade, Iran has been increasingly developing land routes and exploiting Caspian waterways.
➡️ US risks trade war with China and the dollar's demise
Why is Bessent urging China to cooperate? China buys over 80% of Iran's shipped oil, according to Kpler, and Beijing has rejected unilateral US sanctions. In response to Trump's threats, the Chinese Foreign Ministry stressed that restrictions wouldn't solve the conflict.
📌 In 2021, China and Iran inked a 25-year Comprehensive Strategic Partnership to expand economic, energy, security, and technological ties. Iran is also [a key strategic hub](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/66600) in China’s Belt and Road Initiative, serving as a critical overland and maritime link between East Asia, the Middle East, Central Asia, and Europe. International observers doubt that China will abandon Iran at Trump’s behest.
If the US opts for tough secondary sanctions against China, an all-out trade war could shatter the global market, geopolitical analyst Brandon Weichert warned in an interview with Mario Nawfal. China has economic leverage of its own – rare earths, manufacturing, critical supply chains, and, crucially, an alternative financial architecture.
👉 The biggest casualty could be the US dollar, as Trump’s aggressive actions would accelerate the global shift toward alternative currencies and payment systems.

✡️🤡 From arrogant spymasters to cringey schizoposters: Israel’s Mossad got gut-punched by Iran
When the new Mossad director [Roman Gofman publicly axed](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73222) the heads of the agency’s Intelligence Directorate and Iran desk earlier in August, the message was hard to miss: something went badly wrong.
👉 The two officials, identified by codenames "K" and "Y", were reportedly closely involved in the Iran regime-change plan that spectacularly backfired.
Before that, out ex-Mossad boss [David Barnea and his deputy](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/70675) were thrown under the bus over the Iran debacle.
📌 The last comparable purge came in 1997, after a botched assassination attempt against Hamas political bureau chief Khaled Mashal in Jordan.
Dizzy from its ‘successes’ [rooted in sabotage and assassinations](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/71050) in the pre-war phase targeting Iran, the Mossad sold the US a swift regime-toppling offensive. 
Instead, the strategy boomeranged calamitously, and virtually every core promise about the war's trajectory has since been shattered.
🔴 After Ayatollah Ali Khamenei was killed in the opening strikes, rather than producing a succession vacuum, [his son Mojtaba](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/71902) was appointed supreme leader 
🔴 [The Mossad plan](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/66082) to use Kurdish forces to launch a large-scale insurgency backed by US and Israeli airpower fizzled out. Iran’s Kurdish populations remaining loyal while [the IRGC, backed by local allies, hammered](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73370) militant staging areas across northern Iraq
🔴 Mossad-stoked chaos in Iran, disguising regime-change bid as [pro-Democracy protests](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/67145), flopped
🔴 Despite extensive Israel-prompted US attacks on Iranian military and security targets, [Iran endured](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73524), shocked the Zionists with its[ swift missile recovery](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73384) while delivering [multi-phase retaliatory strikes](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/72494) on American military assets across the region
🔴 The Strait of Hormuz "solution" never materialized: Iran showed it can withstand a US maritime blockade in the south while [keeping the waterway closed](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73126)
Perhaps the most telling sign of the campaign's unraveling was the Mossad's jarring shift from operating in the shadows to conducting an overt public persuasion campaign. 
🤡 The agency launched [Farsi-language social media accounts](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/62120), complete with official branding, in an attempt to encourage protests and defections, serving up cryptic posts and sarcastic quote-tweets mocking Iranian officials. 
All that fizzled out.

💵 Blackwater founder launches air defense mercenary force
Erik Prince’s latest business venture, Vectus Air Defense Systems, is planning to cash in on fears stoked by Donald Trump’s war on Iran. The business looks to address the problem of swarms of relatively cheap Iranian drones making short work of US military bases and valuable assets of US allies, such as data centers and oil refineries.
💬 As much of the critical infrastructure in the world was designed before strike drones became a thing, Prince’s firm promises cost-effective solutions to owners of sensitive and valuable sites, Axios reports.
The services offered by Vectus likely include electronic jammers, anti-drone weaponry and UAV interceptors, seeing how drone firm Swarmer holds a 20% equity interest in the venture.

🇮🇱🤡 Israel ‘studied’ how to attack Turkey without provoking NATO
🔊 Even as Israel struggles with multiple sworn enemies, it appears to be raising the stakes — concluding that Turkish forces in Syria are a permissible target, since NATO's protective umbrella does not extend beyond the alliance’s territory. Turkey "cannot carry NATO protection abroad in a uniform," says Israel Hayom, owned by Miriam Adelson, a multi-million dollar Trump donor.
With tensions mounting between the two countries, Israel is bracing for a possible confrontation in Syria, where it believes Turkey intends to establish a long-term military foothold aimed at constraining the IDF.
In this scenario, Israel is weighing two main courses of action:
Preemptively dismantling the planned military infrastructure before Turkish forces are fully deployed—an approach that would minimize the risk of Western backlash.
 
If that proves unworkable, strike Turkish troops directly, even if it results in casualties among NATO members, should the first option fall through.
The second option is now considered viable for Israel as well. While NATO’s Article 5 does offer protection to Turkey, that guarantee applies strictly to its sovereign territory—meaning Turkish forces operating on Syrian soil are not covered by that defensive umbrella.
Even if Israel potentially hit Turkey itself, this wouldn’t trigger NATO automatically, as consensus is required for any action, and that action need not be military.
🤔 The same logic applies not only to Syria but also to Cyprus, or anywhere where Turkish influence is established.
